## Motivation

To improve sglang out-of-box experience on AWS GPU clusters.

## Modifications
Adds AWS EFA variants of the published SGLang CUDA 13 images. Each one is a thin layer over an image that's already published, so `docker/Dockerfile` and the existing release workflows are unchanged.

- **`docker/efa.Dockerfile`**: `FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}`, following the pattern of `docker/sagemaker.Dockerfile`. It adds:
  - The AWS EFA userspace stack: libfabric with the EFA provider, rdma-core and aws-ofi-nccl.
  - On amd64, the EFA Mooncake wheel, pinned to the Mooncake version already in the base image.
  - EFA defaults: `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=efa` (`tcp` on arm64, where the EFA wheel isn't published), `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=LIBFABRIC`, and `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi` / `NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=ofi`.
  - `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/amazon/efa/lib`. With `--gpus`, the NVIDIA container toolkit reruns `ldconfig`, and the rebuilt cache picks the distro libfabric 1.17.0. That copy lacks `FABRIC_1.7`, so NIXL fails with `createBackend: unsupported backend 'LIBFABRIC'`, the same error as on `nightly-dev-20261013-7224fce1`.
  - Build-time checks: the EFA provider is present, every NIXL LIBFABRIC plugin resolves to the AWS libfabric, the ofi-nccl plugins are in the loader cache, and the Mooncake wheel swap leaves exactly one Mooncake package at the expected version.
- **`.github/workflows/release-docker-efa.yml`**: runs after each base workflow succeeds and publishes amd64 + arm64 images:

  | Base | EFA tags |
  |---|---|
  | `v{version}` | `v{version}-efa`, `latest-efa`, `v{version}-cu130-efa`, `latest-cu130-efa` |
  | `v{version}-runtime` | `v{version}-runtime-efa`, `latest-runtime-efa`, `v{version}-cu130-runtime-efa`, `latest-cu130-runtime-efa` |
  | `nightly-dev-{date}-{sha}` | `nightly-dev-efa-{date}-{sha}`, `dev-efa` |

  Nightly EFA tags reuse the base tag's exact `{date}-{sha}` suffix, so each one matches a `nightly-dev-*` image on the same SGLang commit. A `workflow_dispatch` can layer EFA onto any published tag, and old `nightly-dev-efa-*` tags are pruned.
- **`mooncake_store.py`**: when `"protocol"` is missing from the config file or extra config, the store now falls back to `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL.get()` instead of the hard-coded default, so it honors the image's `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=efa`.
- **Docs**: `install.mdx` lists the EFA tags. `pd_disaggregation.mdx` describes what the images contain, the amd64 limits, a `docker run` example with the EFA devices, and how to build `efa.Dockerfile` on a custom base.

Build of `docker/efa.Dockerfile` on a published nightly image (amd64):

```bash
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  --load \
  -f docker/efa.Dockerfile \
  --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-<date>-<sha> \
  --build-arg EFA_IMAGE_TAG=lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-efa-<date>-<sha> \
  -t lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-efa-<date>-<sha> \
  docker/
```

Build of `docker/efa.Dockerfile` on a published latest (amd64):

```
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  --load \
  -f docker/efa.Dockerfile \
  --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=lmsysorg/sglang:latest \
  --build-arg EFA_IMAGE_TAG=lmsysorg/sglang:latest-efa \
  -t lmsysorg/sglang:latest-efa \
  docker/
```

Build of `docker/efa.Dockerfile` on a published latest-runtime (amd64):

```
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  --load \
  -f docker/efa.Dockerfile \
  --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime \
  --build-arg EFA_IMAGE_TAG=lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime-efa \
  -t lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime-efa \
  docker/
```

Worth fixing in this stage (item 2 turned out to be already fixed on main):

1. **NCCL doesn't pick up aws-ofi-nccl by default.** The installer puts `libnccl-ofi-ngc-v3` in `/opt/amazon/ofi-nccl/lib`, which ships only `libnccl-net-ofi.so`/`libnccl-tuner-ofi.so` and no `libnccl-net.so`. NCCL therefore logs `NET/Plugin: Could not find: libnccl-net.so` and falls back to sockets.
   - default: `Using network Socket`, busbw **18.8 GB/s**
   - `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi`: `NET/OFI Initializing aws-ofi-nccl 1.21.1`, `Using network Libfabric`, busbw **404 GB/s**

   Suggest adding `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi` to the stage's `ENV`.

2. ~~**The `runtime` base has no gdrcopy.**~~ *(edited: already fixed on main)* The published `lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime` (built 9/18) is missing `libgdrapi` (`ldd /usr/bin/gdrcopy_sanity` reports `libgdrapi.so.2 => not found`), so libfabric logs `gdrcopy_dl_hmem_init failed!` there. The cause was the runtime stage's COPY source `/usr/lib/libgdrapi.so*`, which main already fixed in #37442 (e047e50d4e, 9/24). After rebasing, `runtime-efa` inherits the fix, so no change is needed in this PR.

Minor: the runtime image has no `torchrun` on `PATH`, so use `python3 -m torch.distributed.run`.

Suggest adding `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi` here. While at it, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` can go, per @erezzarum's comment above: the installer's `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/000_efa.conf` already puts `/opt/amazon/efa/lib` first. I verified that the AWS libfabric is still the one loaded without this ENV.

```suggestion
ENV PATH="/opt/amazon/efa/bin:${PATH}" \
    NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi
```

Why `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN`: the installer puts `libnccl-ofi-ngc-v3` in `/opt/amazon/ofi-nccl/lib`. That package ships only `libnccl-net-ofi.so`/`libnccl-tuner-ofi.so`, with no `libnccl-net.so`, so NCCL's default plugin lookup misses it and falls back to sockets. On 2x p5en.48xlarge, 2x8 GPUs, 512 MiB all_reduce:
- default: `NET/Plugin: Could not find: libnccl-net.so`, `Using network Socket`, busbw 18.8 GB/s
- `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi`: `NET/OFI Initializing aws-ofi-nccl 1.21.1`, `Using network Libfabric`, busbw 404 GB/s

detail.body:
## Motivation

To improve sglang out-of-box experience on AWS GPU clusters.

## Modifications
Adds AWS EFA variants of the published SGLang CUDA 13 images. Each one is a thin layer over an image that's already published, so `docker/Dockerfile` and the existing release workflows are unchanged.

- **`docker/efa.Dockerfile`**: `FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}`, following the pattern of `docker/sagemaker.Dockerfile`. It adds:
  - The AWS EFA userspace stack: libfabric with the EFA provider, rdma-core and aws-ofi-nccl.
  - On amd64, the EFA Mooncake wheel, pinned to the Mooncake version already in the base image.
  - EFA defaults: `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=efa` (`tcp` on arm64, where the EFA wheel isn't published), `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=LIBFABRIC`, and `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi` / `NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=ofi`.
  - `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/amazon/efa/lib`. With `--gpus`, the NVIDIA container toolkit reruns `ldconfig`, and the rebuilt cache picks the distro libfabric 1.17.0. That copy lacks `FABRIC_1.7`, so NIXL fails with `createBackend: unsupported backend 'LIBFABRIC'`, the same error as on `nightly-dev-20261013-7224fce1`.
  - Build-time checks: the EFA provider is present, every NIXL LIBFABRIC plugin resolves to the AWS libfabric, the ofi-nccl plugins are in the loader cache, and the Mooncake wheel swap leaves exactly one Mooncake package at the expected version.
- **`.github/workflows/release-docker-efa.yml`**: runs after each base workflow succeeds and publishes amd64 + arm64 images:

  | Base | EFA tags |
  |---|---|
  | `v{version}` | `v{version}-efa`, `latest-efa`, `v{version}-cu130-efa`, `latest-cu130-efa` |
  | `v{version}-runtime` | `v{version}-runtime-efa`, `latest-runtime-efa`, `v{version}-cu130-runtime-efa`, `latest-cu130-runtime-efa` |
  | `nightly-dev-{date}-{sha}` | `nightly-dev-efa-{date}-{sha}`, `dev-efa` |

  Nightly EFA tags reuse the base tag's exact `{date}-{sha}` suffix, so each one matches a `nightly-dev-*` image on the same SGLang commit. A `workflow_dispatch` can layer EFA onto any published tag, and old `nightly-dev-efa-*` tags are pruned.
- **`mooncake_store.py`**: when `"protocol"` is missing from the config file or extra config, the store now falls back to `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL.get()` instead of the hard-coded default, so it honors the image's `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=efa`.
- **Docs**: `install.mdx` lists the EFA tags. `pd_disaggregation.mdx` describes what the images contain, the amd64 limits, a `docker run` example with the EFA devices, and how to build `efa.Dockerfile` on a custom base.

Build of `docker/efa.Dockerfile` on a published nightly image (amd64):

```bash
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  --load \
  -f docker/efa.Dockerfile \
  --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-<date>-<sha> \
  --build-arg EFA_IMAGE_TAG=lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-efa-<date>-<sha> \
  -t lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-efa-<date>-<sha> \
  docker/
```

Build of `docker/efa.Dockerfile` on a published latest (amd64):

```
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  --load \
  -f docker/efa.Dockerfile \
  --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=lmsysorg/sglang:latest \
  --build-arg EFA_IMAGE_TAG=lmsysorg/sglang:latest-efa \
  -t lmsysorg/sglang:latest-efa \
  docker/
```

Build of `docker/efa.Dockerfile` on a published latest-runtime (amd64):

```
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  --load \
  -f docker/efa.Dockerfile \
  --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime \
  --build-arg EFA_IMAGE_TAG=lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime-efa \
  -t lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime-efa \
  docker/
```

@@ -0,0 +1,287 @@
+name: Release Docker EFA Images
+#
+# Layers docker/efa.Dockerfile on top of already-published images, so the main
+# image workflows and docker/Dockerfile stay untouched. Runs after each base
+# workflow succeeds:
+#
+#   Release Docker Images (tag push)
+#     lmsysorg/sglang:v{version}         -> v{version}-efa, latest-efa,
+#                                           v{version}-cu130-efa, latest-cu130-efa
+#   Release Docker Runtime Images (tag push)
+#     lmsysorg/sglang:v{version}-runtime -> v{version}-runtime-efa, latest-runtime-efa,
+#                                           v{version}-cu130-runtime-efa, latest-cu130-runtime-efa
+#   Build and Push Development Docker Images (schedule or workflow_dispatch)
+#     lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-{date}-{short_sha} -> nightly-dev-efa-{date}-{short_sha}, dev-efa
+#
+# The EFA image inherits the base's SGLang commit and, for nightlies, its exact
+# {date}-{short_sha} suffix, so nightly-dev-efa-X matches nightly-dev-X.
+#
+# A manual dev run publishes a nightly-dev-* tag only when it has no tag or
+# pr_number input; PR and custom-tag builds publish dev-<suffix> instead and
+# are skipped here, since there is no dated nightly to pair with.
+#
+# Manually dispatched release runs are not followed: their inputs (version,
+# image_repo) are not in the workflow_run payload. Use this workflow's own
+# workflow_dispatch for those, and for one-off builds.
+on:
+  workflow_run:
+    workflows:
+      - Release Docker Images
+      - Release Docker Runtime Images
+      - Build and Push Development Docker Images
+    types: [completed]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      base_tag:
+        description: "Published lmsysorg/sglang tag to layer EFA on (e.g. v0.5.21-runtime, nightly-dev-20261013-7224fce1)"
+        required: true
+      output_tags:
+        description: "Comma-separated tags to publish (e.g. v0.5.21-runtime-efa,latest-runtime-efa). Overwrites existing tags."
+        required: true
+      image_repo:
+        description: "Docker Hub repo to push the EFA image to; the base is always pulled from lmsysorg/sglang. Use lmsysorg/sglang-staging for testing."
+        required: false
+        default: "lmsysorg/sglang"
+
+concurrency:
+  # One group per base run (re-runs of it share the id), so only a re-run
+  # supersedes an in-progress EFA build. A coarser key would let one base run
+  # cancel another's EFA build: e.g. a manual PR build of the dev image, which
+  # resolves to skip, would cancel the EFA build for a manual nightly run, and
+  # that day would get no nightly-dev-efa-* at all.
+  group: >-
+    release-docker-efa-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.output_tags ||
+    github.event.workflow_run.id }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+jobs:
+  resolve:
+    if: >-
+      github.repository == 'sgl-project/sglang' &&
+      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
+       (github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
+        (github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' ||
+         github.event.workflow_run.event == 'schedule' ||
+         github.event.workflow_run.event == 'workflow_dispatch')))
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    outputs:
+      skip: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.skip }}
+      nightly: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.nightly }}
+      base_image: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.base_image }}
+      out_images: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.out_images }}
+      primary_image: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.primary_image }}
+      environment: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.environment }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Resolve base image and output tags
+        id: resolve
+        env:
+          # Inject via env so a crafted input or branch name cannot break out
+          # of the script.
+          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
+          SOURCE_WORKFLOW: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.name }}
+          SOURCE_EVENT: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.event }}
+          SOURCE_REF: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
+          SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+          SOURCE_STARTED: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.run_started_at }}
+          INPUT_BASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.base_tag }}
+          INPUT_OUTPUT_TAGS: ${{ inputs.output_tags }}
+          INPUT_IMAGE_REPO: ${{ inputs.image_repo }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+
+          # Whole-string checks. A '^...$' regex anchors per LINE, so a
+          # multi-line value would pass and then inject extra GITHUB_OUTPUT lines.
+          validate_tag() {
+            case "$2" in
+              ""|[!a-zA-Z0-9_]*|*[!a-zA-Z0-9._-]*)
+                echo "::error::${1} '${2}' is not a valid Docker tag"
+                exit 1
+                ;;
+            esac
+          }
+
+          # Bases always come from the published repo. REPO is only where the
+          # EFA image is pushed; workflow_dispatch can point it at e.g.
+          # lmsysorg/sglang-staging, which has no nightly or release bases.
+          BASE_REPO="lmsysorg/sglang"
+          REPO="lmsysorg/sglang"
+          ENVIRONMENT=""
+          NIGHTLY="false"
+          if [ "${EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
+            [ -n "${INPUT_IMAGE_REPO}" ] && REPO="${INPUT_IMAGE_REPO}"
+            case "${REPO}" in
+              ""|*[!a-z0-9._/-]*|/*|*/)
+                echo "::error::'${REPO}' is not a valid Docker Hub repo"
+                exit 1
+                ;;
+            esac
+            BASE_TAG="${INPUT_BASE_TAG}"
+            IFS=',' read -ra OUT_TAGS <<< "${INPUT_OUTPUT_TAGS}"
+          else
+            case "${SOURCE_WORKFLOW}/${SOURCE_EVENT}" in
+              "Release Docker Images/push"|"Release Docker Runtime Images/push")
+                # For tag pushes head_branch is the tag name, e.g. v0.5.21.
+                # Same check as the base release workflows; validate_tag below
+                # rejects anything unusable as a tag.
+                VERSION="${SOURCE_REF#v}"
+                if ! echo "${VERSION}" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'; then
+                  echo "::error::Cannot derive a release version from '${SOURCE_REF}'"
+                  exit 1
+                fi
+                if [ "${SOURCE_WORKFLOW}" = "Release Docker Images" ]; then
+                  FLAVOR=""
+                else
+                  FLAVOR="-runtime"
+                fi
+                BASE_TAG="v${VERSION}${FLAVOR}"
+                OUT_TAGS=("v${VERSION}${FLAVOR}-efa" "latest${FLAVOR}-efa"
+                          "v${VERSION}-cu130${FLAVOR}-efa" "latest-cu130${FLAVOR}-efa")
+                # Match the base release workflows, which publish from `prod`.
+                ENVIRONMENT="prod"
+                ;;
+              "Build and Push Development Docker Images/schedule"|"Build and Push Development Docker Images/workflow_dispatch")
+                # The base nightly tag is nightly-dev-{date}-{short_sha}, where
+                # {date} is taken when its manifest is created. Look the tag up by
+                # commit instead of recomputing the date, so a run that crosses
+                # midnight still finds it and the EFA tag reuses the same suffix.
+                #
+                # Only accept a tag pushed after this base run started, i.e. by
+                # this run. Otherwise a manual PR or custom-tag build dispatched
+                # from a commit that already has a nightly would re-publish that
+                # older nightly, and could move dev-efa back to it. Comparing the
+                # first 19 characters (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) of both ISO 8601
+                # timestamps orders them correctly as strings.
+                SHORT_SHA="${SOURCE_SHA:0:8}"
+                case "${SHORT_SHA}" in
+                  *[!0-9a-f]*|"") echo "::error::Bad head_sha '${SOURCE_SHA}'"; exit 1 ;;
+                esac
+                BASE_TAG=""
+                for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+                  BASE_TAG="$(curl -fsS --retry 3 \
+                    "https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/${BASE_REPO}/tags/?name=-${SHORT_SHA}&page_size=100" \
+                    | jq -r --arg sha "${SHORT_SHA}" --arg since "${SOURCE_STARTED:0:19}" \
+                      '[.results[]
+                        | select(.name | test("^nightly-dev-[0-9]{8}-" + $sha + "$"))
+                        | select(.last_updated[0:19] >= $since)
+                        | .name] | first // empty')" || true
+                  [ -n "${BASE_TAG}" ] && break
+                  sleep 30
+                done
+                if [ -z "${BASE_TAG}" ]; then
+                  if [ "${SOURCE_EVENT}" = "schedule" ]; then
+                    # A successful scheduled run always publishes this tag, so
+                    # its absence is a real problem.
+                    echo "::error::No nightly-dev-<date>-${SHORT_SHA} tag pushed by this run found in ${BASE_REPO}"
+                    exit 1
+                  fi
+                  # Manual run that published no dated nightly here: a PR or
+                  # custom-tag build, build_only, or another image_repo.
+                  echo "No nightly-dev-<date>-${SHORT_SHA} tag pushed by this run in ${BASE_REPO}; nothing to do"
+                  echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+                  exit 0
+                fi
+                SUFFIX="${BASE_TAG#nightly-dev-}"
+                OUT_TAGS=("nightly-dev-efa-${SUFFIX}" "dev-efa")
+                NIGHTLY="true"
+                ;;
+              *)
+                echo "Nothing to do for '${SOURCE_WORKFLOW}' (${SOURCE_EVENT})"
+                echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+                exit 0
+                ;;
+            esac
+          fi
+
+          validate_tag base_tag "${BASE_TAG}"
+          [ "${#OUT_TAGS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || { echo "::error::No output tags"; exit 1; }
+          OUT_IMAGES=""
+          for t in "${OUT_TAGS[@]}"; do
+            t="$(echo "${t}" | xargs)"
+            validate_tag output_tag "${t}"
+            OUT_IMAGES="${OUT_IMAGES:+${OUT_IMAGES} }${REPO}:${t}"
+          done
+
+          echo "Base:    ${BASE_REPO}:${BASE_TAG}"
+          echo "Outputs: ${OUT_IMAGES}"
+          {
+            echo "skip=false"
+            echo "nightly=${NIGHTLY}"
+            echo "base_image=${BASE_REPO}:${BASE_TAG}"
+            echo "out_images=${OUT_IMAGES}"
+            echo "primary_image=${OUT_IMAGES%% *}"
+            echo "environment=${ENVIRONMENT}"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+  build-and-publish:
+    needs: resolve
+    if: needs.resolve.outputs.skip == 'false'
+    # Same runner as patch-docker-dev.yml, which also layers onto published
+    # multi-arch images; it has the disk for both platforms' base layers.
+    runs-on: x64-docker-build-node
+    environment: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.environment || null }}
+    env:
+      BASE_IMAGE: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.base_image }}
+      OUT_IMAGES: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.out_images }}
+      PRIMARY_IMAGE: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.primary_image }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Cleanup workspace (remove root-owned files from prior runs)
+        run: sudo rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/* || true
+
+      # Always the default branch's efa.Dockerfile: older release tags do not
+      # have it, and the layer does not depend on the SGLang source.
+      - name: Checkout repository
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+
+      - name: Set up QEMU
+        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
+
+      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
+        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
+
+      - name: Login to Docker Hub
+        uses: docker/login-action@v2
+        with:
+          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
+          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Build and push EFA image (amd64 + arm64)
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          TAG_ARGS=()
+          for img in ${OUT_IMAGES}; do TAG_ARGS+=(-t "${img}"); done
+          # Each platform layers onto its own arch of the base manifest list, so
+          # the output stays a list. A single-arch base fails here on purpose:
+          # the output would not be pullable on the other arch.
+          docker buildx build \
+            --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
+            --no-cache \
+            -f docker/efa.Dockerfile \
+            --build-arg BASE_IMAGE="${BASE_IMAGE}" \
+            --build-arg EFA_IMAGE_TAG="${PRIMARY_IMAGE}" \
+            "${TAG_ARGS[@]}" \
+            --push \
+            docker/
+
+      - name: Write summary
+        run: |
+          {
+            echo "### Published EFA image"
+            echo "- **Base image:** \`${BASE_IMAGE}\`"
+            for img in ${OUT_IMAGES}; do echo "- \`${img}\`"; done
+            echo "- **Platforms:** \`linux/amd64,linux/arm64\`"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+
+      - name: Clean up
+        if: always()
+        run: docker buildx prune --filter "until=72h" -f || true
+
+  cleanup-nightly:
+    needs: [resolve, build-and-publish]
+    # Any run that published a nightly-dev-efa-* tag, scheduled or manual.
+    if: needs.resolve.outputs.nightly == 'true'
+    uses: ./.github/workflows/_docker-cleanup-nightly.yml
+    with:
+      # The cleanup regex is "^<prefix>-[0-9]", so this never touches the
+      # nightly-dev-<date>-* tags of the base workflow.
+      tag_prefixes: '["nightly-dev-efa"]'
+    secrets: inherit

+# AWS EFA variant of a published CUDA 13 SGLang image: adds the EFA userspace
+# stack, the EFA Mooncake wheel (amd64 only), and EFA defaults for Mooncake,
+# NIXL and NCCL. Published by .github/workflows/release-docker-efa.yml.
+#
+#   docker build -f docker/efa.Dockerfile \
+#       --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime -t sglang:efa docker/
+#
+# The host still provides the EFA kernel module and memlock limits.
+ARG BASE_IMAGE=lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime
+FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}
+
+ARG TARGETARCH
+ARG EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION=1.50.0
+ARG EFA_INSTALLER_SHA256=fa6dff8593d866866c13cb4640d9059835cd4efa427971f100ab40c97bef2841
+
+# Install the AWS EFA userspace stack. The distro libfabric1 stays (libopenmpi
+# depends on it); the ENV below makes the AWS copy win at runtime.
+RUN set -eux; \
+    EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE="/tmp/aws-efa-installer-${EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION}.tar.gz"; \
+    curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors \
+        "https://efa-installer.amazonaws.com/aws-efa-installer-${EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION}.tar.gz" \
+        -o "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}"; \
+    echo "${EFA_INSTALLER_SHA256}  ${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" | sha256sum -c -; \
+    tar -xzf "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" -C /tmp; \
+    # The installer apt-installs dependencies; the base image purged the lists.
+    apt-get update -y; \
+    # Not --minimal: it skips libfabric, which the EFA data path needs.
+    (cd /tmp/aws-efa-installer && \
+        ./efa_installer.sh -y --skip-kmod --skip-limit-conf --no-verify); \
+    test -x /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info; \
+    /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info --version; \
+    # `-l` lists providers without EFA hardware, so this works in a build.
+    /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info -l | grep -q '^efa:'; \
+    ldconfig -p | grep -m1 'libfabric\.so\.1' | grep -q '/opt/amazon/efa/lib/'; \
+    # NIXL's plugin needs FABRIC_1.7, which the distro libfabric 1.17.0 lacks.
+    NIXL_LIBFABRIC_PLUGINS="$(find "$(python3 -c 'import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_paths()["purelib"])')" \
+        -name libplugin_LIBFABRIC.so)"; \
+    test -n "${NIXL_LIBFABRIC_PLUGINS}"; \
+    for plugin in ${NIXL_LIBFABRIC_PLUGINS}; do \
+        ldd "${plugin}" | grep -E '^[[:space:]]*libfabric\.so\.1 => /opt/amazon/efa/lib/'; \
+    done; \
+    # Plugins that NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi and NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=ofi resolve to.
+    ldconfig -p | grep -q '/opt/amazon/ofi-nccl/lib/libnccl-net-ofi\.so$'; \
+    ldconfig -p | grep -q '/opt/amazon/ofi-nccl/lib/libnccl-tuner-ofi\.so$'; \
+    apt-get clean; \
+    rm -rf "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" /tmp/aws-efa-installer \
+        /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# LD_LIBRARY_PATH is required: under `--gpus` the NVIDIA toolkit reruns
+# ldconfig, which puts the distro libfabric first in the cache.
+ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/amazon/efa/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}" \
+    PATH="/opt/amazon/efa/bin:${PATH}" \
+    NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi \
+    NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=ofi
+
+# Swap in the EFA Mooncake wheel at the base image's Mooncake version. Both
+# wheels own the `mooncake` module; it is published for x86_64 only.
+RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip \
+    set -eux; \
+    if [ "${TARGETARCH}" = "amd64" ]; then \
+        pkg_version() { python3 -c 'import importlib.metadata as m, sys; print(m.version(sys.argv[1]))' "$1"; }; \
+        MOONCAKE_VERSION="$(pkg_version mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13)"; \
+        test -n "${MOONCAKE_VERSION}"; \
+        python3 -m pip uninstall -y mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13; \
+        python3 -m pip install --no-deps \
+            "mooncake-transfer-engine-efa-cuda13==${MOONCAKE_VERSION}"; \
+        test "$(pkg_version mooncake-transfer-engine-efa-cuda13)" = "${MOONCAKE_VERSION}"; \
+        # `! cmd` is exempt from `set -e`, so check explicitly.
+        if pkg_version mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13 >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
+            echo "mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13 is still installed" >&2; \
+            exit 1; \
+        fi; \
+    else \
+        echo "TARGETARCH=${TARGETARCH}: mooncake-transfer-engine-efa-cuda13 is \
+x86_64-only, keeping the standard wheel (Mooncake EFA protocol unavailable)"; \
+    fi
+
+# Only amd64 has the EFA Mooncake wheel; other arches use tcp. ENV cannot be
+# conditional, so this is "tcp if TARGETARCH is not amd64, else efa".
+ARG ARCH_IF_NOT_AMD64=${TARGETARCH#amd64}

Adding some Mooncake-side context (I maintain Mooncake's EFA transport). It's actually a bit worse than "won't work over EFA": in the standard wheel, `rdma` auto-discovery also picks up the EFA NICs as verbs devices. The RC QP creation then fails (`Failed to create QP: Operation not supported`) and the transfer hangs instead of falling back. I reproduced this on p5en with the standard wheel. kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4355 makes RDMA skip EFA NICs and fall back to TCP, but it isn't released yet.

On arm64 specifically:

Validated the `runtime-efa` stage on 2x p5en.48xlarge (16 EFA NICs each, H200). The stage from 51ae62e2 was applied as-is on top of `lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime` (0.5.20). Summary:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| build + in-stage assertions (sha256, `fi_info -l`, ldconfig order, wheel swap) | ✅ |
| libfabric 2.6.0amzn from `/opt/amazon/efa`, `SUPPORT_EFA=True`, `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=efa` | ✅ |
| same, with the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` ENV removed (per @erezzarum's comment) | ✅ still resolves the AWS libfabric via `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/000_efa.conf`, so the ENV can go |
| P/D disagg, NIXL + `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=LIBFABRIC` | ✅ (without it NIXL uses UCX, see inline comment) |
| P/D disagg, Mooncake `efa`, default allocator | ✅ |
| Mooncake Store over EFA (DRAM put/get, GPU `put_from`/`get_into` to a remote DRAM segment) | ✅ |
| P/D disagg, Mooncake + `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` | ❌ ofiwg/libfabric#12853 (`SYNC_MEMOPS` NOT_SUPPORTED -> `fi_write` EINVAL). The 0.5.20 base doesn't have #39973's startup guard. |
| NCCL all_reduce 2x8 GPUs, 512 MiB | ⚠️ see 1. below |

Worth fixing in this stage (item 2 turned out to be already fixed on main):

1. **NCCL doesn't pick up aws-ofi-nccl by default.** The installer puts `libnccl-ofi-ngc-v3` in `/opt/amazon/ofi-nccl/lib`, which ships only `libnccl-net-ofi.so`/`libnccl-tuner-ofi.so` and no `libnccl-net.so`. NCCL therefore logs `NET/Plugin: Could not find: libnccl-net.so` and falls back to sockets.
   - default: `Using network Socket`, busbw **18.8 GB/s**
   - `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi`: `NET/OFI Initializing aws-ofi-nccl 1.21.1`, `Using network Libfabric`, busbw **404 GB/s**

   Suggest adding `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi` to the stage's `ENV`.

2. ~~**The `runtime` base has no gdrcopy.**~~ *(edited: already fixed on main)* The published `lmsysorg/sglang:latest-runtime` (built 9/18) is missing `libgdrapi` (`ldd /usr/bin/gdrcopy_sanity` reports `libgdrapi.so.2 => not found`), so libfabric logs `gdrcopy_dl_hmem_init failed!` there. The cause was the runtime stage's COPY source `/usr/lib/libgdrapi.so*`, which main already fixed in #37442 (e047e50d4e, 9/24). After rebasing, `runtime-efa` inherits the fix, so no change is needed in this PR.

Minor: the runtime image has no `torchrun` on `PATH`, so use `python3 -m torch.distributed.run`.

The current diff adds `runtime-efa` only to `release-docker-runtime.yml`, so EFA images would appear only with releases. SemiAnalysis InferenceX AgentX submissions pin dated `nightly-dev-*` images. A release-only EFA tag can't unblock them until the next release, and it would also move them to a different SGLang commit.

Concrete case: the B300 DeepSeek-V4 Dynamo+SGLang disaggregated recipes on AWS EFA use `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=LIBFABRIC`. On `nightly-dev-20261013-7224fce1`, every prefill rank fails at KV-manager init:

```
E1013 05:03:12 nixl_agent.cpp:334] createBackend: unsupported backend 'LIBFABRIC'
nixl_cu13._bindings.nixlNotFoundError: NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND
```

With `NIXL_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`, the cause that NIXL otherwise logs only at INFO is:

```
Failed to load plugin from .../.nixl_cu13.mesonpy.libs/plugins/libplugin_LIBFABRIC.so: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libfabric.so.1: version `FABRIC_1.7' not found
```

The nightly image has only Ubuntu's `libfabric1` 1.17.0, whose newest symbol version is `FABRIC_1.6`. `libplugin_LIBFABRIC.so` in both `nixl-cu13` 1.4.1 and 1.5.0 imports `fi_getinfo@FABRIC_1.7`. The AWS libfabric that this PR's `runtime-efa` stage installs provides it, so a nightly build of that stage would fix this case.
